comparison.objective: Thread and tighten a spin-on oil filter to gasket contact and then to a prescribed turn or 18 N·m; the candidate adjusts and locks a gripper opening stop before cycling it.
comparison.physical_skill: PR-1405 tests grasping and rotating a large threaded can, with later versions seating a cap wrench and applying ratchet torque. The candidate tests fine coaxial driver engagement plus a separate open-ended wrench on a thin nut while counterholding the adjustment screw.
comparison.success_condition: PR-1405 grades final rotation past gasket contact, penalizes loose, removed, or overcrushed filters, and requires release and wrench removal in later versions. The candidate grades retained 90° opening, nut retention, three motion cycles, drift, and clearance. No material rubric details are missing across the recorded versions.
comparison.reason: Threaded tightening and tool release are shared primitives, but PR-1405 does not test preserving an independently adjustable stop against locknut reaction or validating that setting through repeated articulated cycles.
